Article 5
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and the community are implemented in the form of participation.
(2) The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. Preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. Providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. Participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.
(3) The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (2) are implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 7
Letter a What is meant by "Non-Physical Violence" is statements, gestures, or activities that are improper and lead to violence with the purpose of demeaning or humiliating.
Letter b What is meant by "Physical Violence" is an act that results in pain, falling ill, or serious injury.
Letter c What is meant by "Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence" is any act that meets the elements of a criminal act as regulated in this regional regulation and other acts of sexual violence as regulated in the Law.
Letter d What is meant by "economic violence" is acts of exploitation, manipulation and control through economic means in the form of forcing victims to work in an exploitative manner, including prostitution, and neglect.
Letter e What is meant by "social violence" is any action with social impact that threatens the physical, mental integrity, or relationships of a person or group, such actions are carried out by a subject or by society itself.
Letter f What is meant by "domestic neglect" is a neglect of a person's obligations within their household where legally that person is responsible for life within the family scope.
Letter g What is meant by "coercion or deprivation of liberty" is deprivation of liberty or deprivation of freedom physically or otherwise arbitrarily that violates the basic provisions of international law, torture, rape, sexual slavery, forced prostitution.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are: a. To prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. To provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence;
c. To provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence;
d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. Through the regulation of protection for Women and Children, it is expected that all parties can better implement the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their protection so that it can be carried out more comprehensively, in an integrated and sustainable manner by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to the protection efforts for Women and Children.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts to implement protection for women and children, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in North Konawe Regency.

Article 13
(1) Special Protection is provided to Children in emergency situations which include:
a. child refugees;
b. children victims of natural disasters; and
c. children victims of unrest.
(2) The handling of special protection for Children in emergency situations as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in a coordinated manner between the Provincial Government, Regency/City and the community.
(3) The handling of child refugees as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out without regard to citizenship status and they have the right to receive basic services.
(4) The handling of Children as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b and letter c includes proper housing, physical and psychological recovery, fulfillment of nutrition, education, health, children's play areas, and prevention from violence and exploitation.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is North Konawe Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of North Konawe Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of North Konawe.
4. State Civil Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as ASN is a profession for civil servants and government employees with work agreements who work in government agencies.
5. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, a child still in the womb, a child with special needs, a child victim, a child perpetrator and a child as a Witness.
7. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
8. Implementation is the execution of something done to achieve a goal.
9. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect women and children and their rights so that they can live, grow, and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
10. Trafficking in Women and Children is the act of recruitment, sheltering, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
11. Special Protection is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
12. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
13. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
14. Community is families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, individuals who have expertise, concern and sincerity to help and social organizations that are potential and strategic as well as legal.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as UPTD PPA is a service provider institution for the protection of women and children victims of violence established and under the Regional Government.
16. North Konawe Regency Child Protection Committee is a supervisory institution for the implementation of Child Protection in North Konawe Regency whose members consist of various elements namely religious leaders, community leaders, related PD and Social Organizations.
17. Regional Children's Forum is a forum for Children to gather, express and have their opinions heard, as well as seek, receive and convey information.
18. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
19. Child-Friendly School is an educational institution that recognizes and respects the rights of children to obtain education, health, opportunities to play and have fun, protection from violence and abuse, ability to express views freely, and participate in decision-making according to their capacity.
20. Child-Friendly Health Services are hospital services that pay attention to aspects of child growth and development by providing child-friendly officers or doctors and child-friendly facilities.
21. Services are activities or series of service activities in the context of implementing the protection of Women and Children in accordance with laws and regulations.

Part Three
Prevention of Violence against Women and Children

Article 14
(1) Special protection is provided to Children dealing with the law, including:
a. children as perpetrators of criminal acts;
b. children as victims of criminal acts; and
c. children as witnesses of criminal acts.
(2) The Regional Government is obligated to provide protection and facilities for Children dealing with the law.
(3) Protection and facilities as referred to in paragraph (2) include:
a. protection from negative labeling, publication, threats and other forms that harm Children;
b. facilities for physical and psychological health services, education and training, safe housing or social homes for Child protection;
c. providing professional and trained companions/service officers in assisting Child cases; and
d. providing special service units in the form of social protection homes for Children.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 22
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of the protection of women and children.
(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. mentoring/assistance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of the protection of women and children in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by regional apparatus/related institutions and the community.
(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be conducted with professional and transparent principles.
(5) The relevant service/department is obligated to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of the protection of women and children.

CHAPTER VIII
FINANCING
Article 21
Funds for the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence are sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. other legitimate sources.

Article 9
(1) In order to provide protection to victims, the Regional Government establishes UPTD PPA as a Regional Technical Implementation Unit within the unit responsible for the Protection of Women and Children.
(2) The establishment of UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, organizational structure, and working procedures of UPTD PPA shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

Letter b What is meant by "Physical Violence" is an act that results in pain, falling ill, or serious injury.
Letter c What is meant by "Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence" is any act that meets the elements of a criminal act as regulated in this regional regulation and other acts of sexual violence as regulated in the Law.
Letter d What is meant by "economic violence" is acts of exploitation, manipulation and control through economic means in the form of forcing victims to work in an exploitative manner, including prostitution, and neglect.
Letter e What is meant by "social violence" is any action with social impact that threatens the physical, mental integrity, or relationships of a person or group, such actions are carried out by a subject or by society itself.

(1) Special protection is provided to Children dealing with the law, including:

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are: a. To prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. To provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence;
c. To provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence;
d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. Through the regulation of protection for Women and Children, it is expected that all parties can better implement the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their protection so that it can be carried out more comprehensively, in an integrated and sustainable manner by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to the protection efforts for Women and Children.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts to implement protection for women and children, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in North Konawe Regency.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are: a. To prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. To provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence;
c. To provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence;
d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. Through the regulation of protection for Women and Children, it is expected that all parties can better implement the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their protection so that it can be carried out more comprehensively, in an integrated and sustainable manner by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to the protection efforts for Women and Children.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts to implement protection for women and children, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in North Konawe Regency.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 22
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of the protection of women and children.
(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:

b. mentoring/assistance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of the protection of women and children in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by regional apparatus/related institutions and the community.
(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be conducted with professional and transparent principles.
(5) The relevant service/department is obligated to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of the protection of women and children.

Article 14

d. providing special service units in the form of social protection homes for Children.

a. child refugees;
b. children victims of natural disasters; and
c. children victims of unrest.
(2) The handling of special protection for Children in emergency situations as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in a coordinated manner between the Provincial Government, Regency/City and the community.

Funds for the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence are sourced from:

7. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
8. Implementation is the execution of something done to achieve a goal.

10. Trafficking in Women and Children is the act of recruitment, sheltering, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
11. Special Protection is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
12. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are: a. To prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. To provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence;
c. To provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence;
d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. Through the regulation of protection for Women and Children, it is expected that all parties can better implement the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their protection so that it can be carried out more comprehensively, in an integrated and sustainable manner by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to the protection efforts for Women and Children.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts to implement protection for women and children, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in North Konawe Regency.

FINANCING

Funds for the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence are sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. other legitimate sources.

I. GENERAL

f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are: a. To prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. To provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence;
c. To provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence;
d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. Through the regulation of protection for Women and Children, it is expected that all parties can better implement the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their protection so that it can be carried out more comprehensively, in an integrated and sustainable manner by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to the protection efforts for Women and Children.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts to implement protection for women and children, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in North Konawe Regency.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are: a. To prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. To provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence;

d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is North Konawe Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of North Konawe Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of North Konawe.
4. State Civil Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as ASN is a profession for civil servants and government employees with work agreements who work in government agencies.
5. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, a child still in the womb, a child with special needs, a child victim, a child perpetrator and a child as a Witness.
7. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
8. Implementation is the execution of something done to achieve a goal.
9. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect women and children and their rights so that they can live, grow, and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
10. Trafficking in Women and Children is the act of recruitment, sheltering, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
11. Special Protection is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
12. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
13. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
14. Community is families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, individuals who have expertise, concern and sincerity to help and social organizations that are potential and strategic as well as legal.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as UPTD PPA is a service provider institution for the protection of women and children victims of violence established and under the Regional Government.
16. North Konawe Regency Child Protection Committee is a supervisory institution for the implementation of Child Protection in North Konawe Regency whose members consist of various elements namely religious leaders, community leaders, related PD and Social Organizations.
17. Regional Children's Forum is a forum for Children to gather, express and have their opinions heard, as well as seek, receive and convey information.
18. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
19. Child-Friendly School is an educational institution that recognizes and respects the rights of children to obtain education, health, opportunities to play and have fun, protection from violence and abuse, ability to express views freely, and participate in decision-making according to their capacity.
20. Child-Friendly Health Services are hospital services that pay attention to aspects of child growth and development by providing child-friendly officers or doctors and child-friendly facilities.
21. Services are activities or series of service activities in the context of implementing the protection of Women and Children in accordance with laws and regulations.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are: a. To prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. To provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence;
c. To provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence;
d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. Through the regulation of protection for Women and Children, it is expected that all parties can better implement the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their protection so that it can be carried out more comprehensively, in an integrated and sustainable manner by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to the protection efforts for Women and Children.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts to implement protection for women and children, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in North Konawe Regency.

Letter a What is meant by "Non-Physical Violence" is statements, gestures, or activities that are improper and lead to violence with the purpose of demeaning or humiliating.
Letter b What is meant by "Physical Violence" is an act that results in pain, falling ill, or serious injury.
Letter c What is meant by "Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence" is any act that meets the elements of a criminal act as regulated in this regional regulation and other acts of sexual violence as regulated in the Law.
Letter d What is meant by "economic violence" is acts of exploitation, manipulation and control through economic means in the form of forcing victims to work in an exploitative manner, including prostitution, and neglect.
Letter e What is meant by "social violence" is any action with social impact that threatens the physical, mental integrity, or relationships of a person or group, such actions are carried out by a subject or by society itself.
Letter f What is meant by "domestic neglect" is a neglect of a person's obligations within their household where legally that person is responsible for life within the family scope.
Letter g What is meant by "coercion or deprivation of liberty" is deprivation of liberty or deprivation of freedom physically or otherwise arbitrarily that violates the basic provisions of international law, torture, rape, sexual slavery, forced prostitution.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are: a. To prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. To provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence;
c. To provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence;
d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. Through the regulation of protection for Women and Children, it is expected that all parties can better implement the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their protection so that it can be carried out more comprehensively, in an integrated and sustainable manner by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to the protection efforts for Women and Children.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts to implement protection for women and children, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in North Konawe Regency.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is North Konawe Regency.

10. Trafficking in Women and Children is the act of recruitment, sheltering, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.

18. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
19. Child-Friendly School is an educational institution that recognizes and respects the rights of children to obtain education, health, opportunities to play and have fun, protection from violence and abuse, ability to express views freely, and participate in decision-making according to their capacity.
20. Child-Friendly Health Services are hospital services that pay attention to aspects of child growth and development by providing child-friendly officers or doctors and child-friendly facilities.
21. Services are activities or series of service activities in the context of implementing the protection of Women and Children in accordance with laws and regulations.

Letter a What is meant by "Non-Physical Violence" is statements, gestures, or activities that are improper and lead to violence with the purpose of demeaning or humiliating.

Letter e What is meant by "social violence" is any action with social impact that threatens the physical, mental integrity, or relationships of a person or group, such actions are carried out by a subject or by society itself.
Letter f What is meant by "domestic neglect" is a neglect of a person's obligations within their household where legally that person is responsible for life within the family scope.
Letter g What is meant by "coercion or deprivation of liberty" is deprivation of liberty or deprivation of freedom physically or otherwise arbitrarily that violates the basic provisions of international law, torture, rape, sexual slavery, forced prostitution.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are: a. To prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. To provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence;
c. To provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence;
d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. Through the regulation of protection for Women and Children, it is expected that all parties can better implement the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their protection so that it can be carried out more comprehensively, in an integrated and sustainable manner by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to the protection efforts for Women and Children.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts to implement protection for women and children, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in North Konawe Regency.

Article 7
Letter a What is meant by "Non-Physical Violence" is statements, gestures, or activities that are improper and lead to violence with the purpose of demeaning or humiliating.
Letter b What is meant by "Physical Violence" is an act that results in pain, falling ill, or serious injury.
Letter c What is meant by "Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence" is any act that meets the elements of a criminal act as regulated in this regional regulation and other acts of sexual violence as regulated in the Law.
Letter d What is meant by "economic violence" is acts of exploitation, manipulation and control through economic means in the form of forcing victims to work in an exploitative manner, including prostitution, and neglect.
Letter e What is meant by "social violence" is any action with social impact that threatens the physical, mental integrity, or relationships of a person or group, such actions are carried out by a subject or by society itself.
Letter f What is meant by "domestic neglect" is a neglect of a person's obligations within their household where legally that person is responsible for life within the family scope.
Letter g What is meant by "coercion or deprivation of liberty" is deprivation of liberty or deprivation of freedom physically or otherwise arbitrarily that violates the basic provisions of international law, torture, rape, sexual slavery, forced prostitution.

2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of North Konawe Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of North Konawe.
4. State Civil Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as ASN is a profession for civil servants and government employees with work agreements who work in government agencies.
5. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, a child still in the womb, a child with special needs, a child victim, a child perpetrator and a child as a Witness.
7. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
8. Implementation is the execution of something done to achieve a goal.
9. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect women and children and their rights so that they can live, grow, and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
10. Trafficking in Women and Children is the act of recruitment, sheltering, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
11. Special Protection is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
12. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
13. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
14. Community is families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, individuals who have expertise, concern and sincerity to help and social organizations that are potential and strategic as well as legal.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as UPTD PPA is a service provider institution for the protection of women and children victims of violence established and under the Regional Government.
16. North Konawe Regency Child Protection Committee is a supervisory institution for the implementation of Child Protection in North Konawe Regency whose members consist of various elements namely religious leaders, community leaders, related PD and Social Organizations.
17. Regional Children's Forum is a forum for Children to gather, express and have their opinions heard, as well as seek, receive and convey information.
18. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
19. Child-Friendly School is an educational institution that recognizes and respects the rights of children to obtain education, health, opportunities to play and have fun, protection from violence and abuse, ability to express views freely, and participate in decision-making according to their capacity.
20. Child-Friendly Health Services are hospital services that pay attention to aspects of child growth and development by providing child-friendly officers or doctors and child-friendly facilities.
21. Services are activities or series of service activities in the context of implementing the protection of Women and Children in accordance with laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 22
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of the protection of women and children.
(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. mentoring/assistance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of the protection of women and children in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by regional apparatus/related institutions and the community.
(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be conducted with professional and transparent principles.
(5) The relevant service/department is obligated to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of the protection of women and children.

Fourth Part
Special Protection of Children

Article 9
(1) In order to provide protection to victims, the Regional Government establishes UPTD PPA as a Regional Technical Implementation Unit within the unit responsible for the Protection of Women and Children.
(2) The establishment of UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, organizational structure, and working procedures of UPTD PPA shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

CHAPTER VIII
FINANCING
Article 21
Funds for the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence are sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. other legitimate sources.

Part Three
Prevention of Violence against Women and Children

Article 14
(1) Special protection is provided to Children dealing with the law, including:
a. children as perpetrators of criminal acts;
b. children as victims of criminal acts; and
c. children as witnesses of criminal acts.
(2) The Regional Government is obligated to provide protection and facilities for Children dealing with the law.
(3) Protection and facilities as referred to in paragraph (2) include:
a. protection from negative labeling, publication, threats and other forms that harm Children;
b. facilities for physical and psychological health services, education and training, safe housing or social homes for Child protection;
c. providing professional and trained companions/service officers in assisting Child cases; and
d. providing special service units in the form of social protection homes for Children.

Article 5
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and the community are implemented in the form of participation.
(2) The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. Preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. Providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. Participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.
(3) The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (2) are implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 13
(1) Special Protection is provided to Children in emergency situations which include:
a. child refugees;
b. children victims of natural disasters; and
c. children victims of unrest.
(2) The handling of special protection for Children in emergency situations as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in a coordinated manner between the Provincial Government, Regency/City and the community.
(3) The handling of child refugees as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out without regard to citizenship status and they have the right to receive basic services.
(4) The handling of Children as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b and letter c includes proper housing, physical and psychological recovery, fulfillment of nutrition, education, health, children's play areas, and prevention from violence and exploitation.

Letter f What is meant by "domestic neglect" is a neglect of a person's obligations within their household where legally that person is responsible for life within the family scope.
Letter g What is meant by "coercion or deprivation of liberty" is deprivation of liberty or deprivation of freedom physically or otherwise arbitrarily that violates the basic provisions of international law, torture, rape, sexual slavery, forced prostitution.

REGARDING

I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.

c. To provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence;
d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. Through the regulation of protection for Women and Children, it is expected that all parties can better implement the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their protection so that it can be carried out more comprehensively, in an integrated and sustainable manner by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to the protection efforts for Women and Children.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are: a. To prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. To provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence;
c. To provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence;
d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. Through the regulation of protection for Women and Children, it is expected that all parties can better implement the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their protection so that it can be carried out more comprehensively, in an integrated and sustainable manner by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to the protection efforts for Women and Children.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts to implement protection for women and children, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in North Konawe Regency.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are: a. To prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. To provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence;
c. To provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence;
d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. Through the regulation of protection for Women and Children, it is expected that all parties can better implement the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their protection so that it can be carried out more comprehensively, in an integrated and sustainable manner by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to the protection efforts for Women and Children.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts to implement protection for women and children, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in North Konawe Regency.

This Regional Regulation regulates efforts to implement protection for women and children, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in North Konawe Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Region is North Konawe Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of North Konawe Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of North Konawe.
4. State Civil Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as ASN is a profession for civil servants and government employees with work agreements who work in government agencies.
5. Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
6. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, a child still in the womb, a child with special needs, a child victim, a child perpetrator and a child as a Witness.
7. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
8. Implementation is the execution of something done to achieve a goal.
9. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to guarantee and protect women and children and their rights so that they can live, grow, and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect.
10. Trafficking in Women and Children is the act of recruitment, sheltering, sending, transferring or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
11. Special Protection is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
12. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
13. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
14. Community is families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, individuals who have expertise, concern and sincerity to help and social organizations that are potential and strategic as well as legal.
15. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter referred to as UPTD PPA is a service provider institution for the protection of women and children victims of violence established and under the Regional Government.
16. North Konawe Regency Child Protection Committee is a supervisory institution for the implementation of Child Protection in North Konawe Regency whose members consist of various elements namely religious leaders, community leaders, related PD and Social Organizations.
17. Regional Children's Forum is a forum for Children to gather, express and have their opinions heard, as well as seek, receive and convey information.
18. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
19. Child-Friendly School is an educational institution that recognizes and respects the rights of children to obtain education, health, opportunities to play and have fun, protection from violence and abuse, ability to express views freely, and participate in decision-making according to their capacity.
20. Child-Friendly Health Services are hospital services that pay attention to aspects of child growth and development by providing child-friendly officers or doctors and child-friendly facilities.
21. Services are activities or series of service activities in the context of implementing the protection of Women and Children in accordance with laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 22
(1) The Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of the protection of women and children.
(2) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. mentoring/assistance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
(3) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of the protection of women and children in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by regional apparatus/related institutions and the community.
(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be conducted with professional and transparent principles.
(5) The relevant service/department is obligated to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of the protection of women and children.

Article 7
Letter a What is meant by "Non-Physical Violence" is statements, gestures, or activities that are improper and lead to violence with the purpose of demeaning or humiliating.
Letter b What is meant by "Physical Violence" is an act that results in pain, falling ill, or serious injury.
Letter c What is meant by "Criminal Acts of Sexual Violence" is any act that meets the elements of a criminal act as regulated in this regional regulation and other acts of sexual violence as regulated in the Law.
Letter d What is meant by "economic violence" is acts of exploitation, manipulation and control through economic means in the form of forcing victims to work in an exploitative manner, including prostitution, and neglect.
Letter e What is meant by "social violence" is any action with social impact that threatens the physical, mental integrity, or relationships of a person or group, such actions are carried out by a subject or by society itself.
Letter f What is meant by "domestic neglect" is a neglect of a person's obligations within their household where legally that person is responsible for life within the family scope.
Letter g What is meant by "coercion or deprivation of liberty" is deprivation of liberty or deprivation of freedom physically or otherwise arbitrarily that violates the basic provisions of international law, torture, rape, sexual slavery, forced prostitution.

Article 5
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and the community are implemented in the form of participation.
(2) The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. Preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. Providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or the competent authorities; and
c. Participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.
(3) The forms of participation of the private sector and the community as referred to in paragraph (2) are implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 9
(1) In order to provide protection to victims, the Regional Government establishes UPTD PPA as a Regional Technical Implementation Unit within the unit responsible for the Protection of Women and Children.
(2) The establishment of UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, organizational structure, and working procedures of UPTD PPA shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

Fourth Part
Special Protection of Children

Article 14
(1) Special protection is provided to Children dealing with the law, including:
a. children as perpetrators of criminal acts;
b. children as victims of criminal acts; and
c. children as witnesses of criminal acts.
(2) The Regional Government is obligated to provide protection and facilities for Children dealing with the law.
(3) Protection and facilities as referred to in paragraph (2) include:
a. protection from negative labeling, publication, threats and other forms that harm Children;
b. facilities for physical and psychological health services, education and training, safe housing or social homes for Child protection;
c. providing professional and trained companions/service officers in assisting Child cases; and
d. providing special service units in the form of social protection homes for Children.

Article 13
(1) Special Protection is provided to Children in emergency situations which include:
a. child refugees;
b. children victims of natural disasters; and
c. children victims of unrest.
(2) The handling of special protection for Children in emergency situations as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in a coordinated manner between the Provincial Government, Regency/City and the community.
(3) The handling of child refugees as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out without regard to citizenship status and they have the right to receive basic services.
(4) The handling of Children as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b and letter c includes proper housing, physical and psychological recovery, fulfillment of nutrition, education, health, children's play areas, and prevention from violence and exploitation.

Part Three
Prevention of Violence against Women and Children

FINANCING
Article 21
Funds for the implementation of protection for Women and Children from acts of violence are sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. other legitimate sources.

Article 24
UPTD PPA or safe houses are prohibited from collecting fees in providing services to women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are: a. To prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. To provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence;
c. To provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence;
d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. Through the regulation of protection for Women and Children, it is expected that all parties can better implement the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their protection so that it can be carried out more comprehensively, in an integrated and sustainable manner by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to the protection efforts for Women and Children.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts to implement protection for women and children, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in North Konawe Regency.

Part One
Regional Government

Article 17
(1) Children with special needs have the right to receive the same treatment as other children to develop their potential in accordance with their dignity and worth.
(2) The regional government is obligated to provide educational and health facilities and infrastructure.
(3) The regional government is obligated to provide rehabilitation centers that include rehabilitation for children and strengthening for Families.
(4) The Regional Government facilitates the establishment of a Communication Forum for Families of Children with Special Needs.

Article 13
(1) Special Protection is provided to Children in emergency situations which include:
a. child refugees;
b. children victims of natural disasters; and
c. children victims of unrest.
(2) The handling of special protection for Children in emergency situations as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in a coordinated manner between the Provincial Government, Regency/City and the community.
(3) The handling of child refugees as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is carried out without regard to citizenship status and they have the right to receive basic services.
(4) The handling of Children as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b and letter c includes proper housing, physical and psychological recovery, fulfillment of nutrition, education, health, children's play areas, and prevention from violence and exploitation.

REGARDING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Every human being has equal rights in living life. The State has the obligation to provide protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That women and children are vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.
Women and children are vulnerable groups who have special needs that are at risk due to physical, psychological, social, cultural and health conditions. In order to realize general welfare in accordance with its authority, the Regional Government is obligated to provide protection to Women and Children.
The objectives of implementing protection for women and children are: a. To prevent all forms of violence against women and children; b. To provide protection and services to women and children victims of violence;
c. To provide a sense of security to women and children victims of violence;
d. To restore the physical, psychological and economic condition of women and children victims of violence;
e. The best interests of women and children victims of violence that occurs in the domestic and/or public sphere; and
f. To take action against perpetrators of violence against women and children. Through the regulation of protection for Women and Children, it is expected that all parties can better implement the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their protection so that it can be carried out more comprehensively, in an integrated and sustainable manner by government elements, families and communities as well as other institutions related to the protection efforts for Women and Children.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts to implement protection for women and children, particularly in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of women and children victims of violence in North Konawe Regency.

Article 14
(1) Special protection is provided to Children dealing with the law, including:
a. children as perpetrators of criminal acts;
b. children as victims of criminal acts; and
c. children as witnesses of criminal acts.
(2) The Regional Government is obligated to provide protection and facilities for Children dealing with the law.
(3) Protection and facilities as referred to in paragraph (2) include:
a. protection from negative labeling, publication, threats and other forms that harm Children;
b. facilities for physical and psychological health services, education and training, safe housing or social homes for Child protection;
c. providing professional and trained companions/service officers in assisting Child cases; and
d. providing special service units in the form of social protection homes for Children.

Article 9
(1) In order to provide protection to victims, the Regional Government establishes UPTD PPA as a Regional Technical Implementation Unit within the unit responsible for the Protection of Women and Children.
(2) The establishment of UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, organizational structure, and working procedures of UPTD PPA shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.
